review_candidates.description: AI Engineer & Technical Co-Founder — Owlera About Owlera Owlera is an AI-powered career and professional experience platform built to solve one of the biggest challenges facing students and early-career talent: you need experience to get opportunities, but you need opportunities to gain experience. We turn real company work into immersive virtual simulated internships where students complete professional missions, work with company resources, interact with AI managers, receive feedback and evaluation, and build verified evidence of what they can actually do. Our vision goes beyond courses and traditional job simulations. We are building an AI-powered environment where people can build experience, prove their abilities, and prepare for a rapidly changing world of work. About the Opportunity We are looking for an exceptional AI Engineer to join Owlera as a technical co-founder/founding technical partner and take ownership of the AI intelligence behind the platform. This is not a role focused on simply connecting an application to an LLM API. We need someone who can architect and build production AI systems that become core parts of the Owlera experience. You would work directly with the founder to transform our validated MVP into a scalable AI-powered platform and help shape both the product and technical direction of the company. What You'll Do You will design and build Owlera's AI architecture and core AI product capabilities, including: • AI agents and multi-step agentic workflows • AI Managers and Supervisors that guide students through realistic work experiences • AI evaluators that assess student submissions, provide feedback, score performance, and identify skills and professional behaviors • RAG systems that allow AI agents to understand company documents, resources, processes, and internship context • LLM integrations, orchestration, tool calling, memory, context management, and structured outputs • Conversational AI and intelligent chat experiences • AI-powered internship and mission generation from real company information • Career intelligence and personalized AI guidance • Reliable evaluation pipelines, guardrails, monitoring, testing, and AI quality improvement • Backend integrations required to connect these AI systems with the wider Owlera product You will also help determine what should be handled by agents, traditional software, retrieval systems, workflows, or other AI approaches as the platform scales. What We're Looking For We are looking for someone who is both a strong AI engineer and a builder. You should have hands-on experience with LLM applications, AI agents, agentic workflows, RAG, embeddings/vector databases, tool calling, structured outputs, prompt and context engineering, and production AI systems. Experience with Python and modern backend development is important. Full-stack experience is a major advantage because this is an early-stage company where technical ownership will extend beyond isolated AI models. Most importantly, we want someone who thinks like a founder: someone comfortable with ambiguity, fast experimentation, technical ownership, product decisions, and building from an early stage. Experience in EdTech, HRTech, Future of Work, assessment systems, recommendation systems, or AI evaluation is valuable but not required. Important: This Is a Co-Founder Opportunity This is not a salaried position at this stage. Owlera is currently pre-seed and raising capital. We are looking for a technical partner who believes in the problem and wants to help build the company from the ground up in exchange for co-founder equity, with compensation becoming possible as the company raises funding and grows. This opportunity is best suited for someone who wants more than their next engineering job. We are looking for someone who wants to help build the technology, product, team, and company alongside the founder. Learn more about Owlera: www.owlera.online

review_candidates.title: Lead Learning Experience Designer
review_candidates.description: The Wikimedia Foundation is seeking a Lead Learning Experience Designer to create innovative, engaging, and accessible learning experiences that strengthen the capacity of volunteers and communities across the Wikimedia movement. You'll help contributors develop the confidence, skills, and knowledge they need to participate effectively, navigate Wikimedia’s communities and practices, and grow as contributors. In this role, you'll partner with Foundation teams, affiliates, researchers, subject matter experts, and volunteers to understand learner needs, identify barriers to participation, and develop learning experiences that support contributors at different stages of their journey. This role goes beyond traditional instructional design. You’ll think like a learning product designer, finding the right approach for each challenge, whether that means creating an online course on Wikimedia’s learning management system (LMS), WikiLearn, producing multimedia content, experimenting with emerging technologies, or embedding learning into existing experiences and workflows. You will do all this while ensuring the experiences you create are culturally responsive, accessible, and relevant to a global audience. This role is intended for an experienced individual who is comfortable operating with a high degree of autonomy and making decisions in complex, evolving environments. Success in this role means being a curious, resourceful problem solver who understands how people learn, grow, and participate. You can think big about how learning can strengthen the Wikimedia movement, while also rolling up your sleeves to build, experiment, and iterate on solutions that make a meaningful difference. Responsibilities Design and develop innovative digital learning experiences, capacity-strengthening resources, and performance support solutions for contributors across the Wikimedia movement. Partner with product teams, community groups, researchers, and subject matter experts to identify learning needs, contributor challenges, and opportunities to strengthen participation. Determine the right learning approach for each opportunity, whether that be a self-paced course, video, interactive experience, AI-enabled support, workshop, or embedded guidance. Develop learning experiences that support contributors in understanding new tools, workflows, policies, governance processes, and community practices across Wikimedia projects. Rapidly prototype, test and iterate on learning experiences, using modern authoring tools, multimedia, and AI tools. Apply learning science, user-centered design, and learning experience design methodologies to create engaging, effective, and inclusive solutions. Evaluate learning effectiveness using learner feedback, participation data, and other qualitative and quantitative insights, continuously improving content based on evidence and community feedback. Contribute to the ongoing evolution of the Foundation's learning strategy by staying current with learning technology, online learning, AI, and digital engagement, identifying opportunities to expand and strengthen learning offerings across the movement. Ensure learning resources reflect Wikimedia's values of openness, collaboration, equity, and knowledge sharing. Qualifications Required Experience designing and developing digital learning experiences for diverse, global audiences. Demonstrated experience creating engaging e-learning, instructor-led, virtual, or blended learning solutions. Experience using a learning management system (LMS) to develop, organize, and publish learning content. Demonstrated ability to diagnose capability gaps, identify the right interventions, and rapidly design, build and improve learning experiences. Excellent written communication and content development skills, with the ability to simplify complex concepts for diverse audiences. Experience collaborating with cross-functional stakeholders and subject matter experts. Commitment to accessibility, inclusive design, and culturally responsive learning practices. Preferred Experience working with volunteer communities, open knowledge initiatives, nonprofits, or international organizations. Experience designing learning for multilingual audiences and collaborating across cultures and time zones. Experience creating learning in modern digital environments using tools such as Rise, Storyline, Camtasia, Adobe Creative Suite, Figma, video editing tools, AI content generation platforms, or similar technologies. Experience partnering with product teams or using product design approaches, such as user research, experimentation, prototyping and iteration. Knowledge of experimentation methods, A/B testing, learning analytics, product analytics, and continuous improvement practices. Familiarity with Wikimedia projects, the Wikimedia movement, or open-source communities. You'll Thrive in This Role If You... Think like a designer and builder, comfortable moving from identifying challenges to creating, testing and improving solutions. Are curious about how people learn, what motivates participation, and how to leverage modern methods and technology to create memorable learning experiences. Are energized by ambiguity and enjoy figuring out what needs to be built rather than waiting for a predefined assignment. Excel at collaborating with people from different backgrounds, languages, and areas of expertise. Balance creativity with evidence and structure, using data, research, and feedback to guide decisions. Care deeply about accessibility, inclusion, and creating learning that supports equitable participation. Are inspired by Wikimedia's mission to make knowledge freely available to everyone. About The Wikimedia Foundation The Wikimedia Foundation is the nonprofit organization that operates Wikipedia and the other Wikimedia free knowledge projects. Our vision is a world in which every single human can freely share in the sum of all knowledge. We believe that everyone has the potential to contribute something to our shared knowledge, and that everyone should be able to access that knowledge freely. We host Wikipedia and the Wikimedia projects, build software experiences for reading, contributing, and sharing Wikimedia content, support the volunteer communities and partners who make Wikimedia possible, and advocate for policies that enable Wikimedia and free knowledge to thrive. The Wikimedia Foundation is a charitable, not-for-profit organization that relies on donations. We receive donations from millions of individuals around the world, with an average donation of about $15. We also receive donations through institutional grants and gifts.
